rv.q: Memoirs of Amorous Gentlemen isn't the next great American musical, but it does at least represent a maturing sensibility around sex workers and the men who hire them.

Like Caruso and Jeacoma in 'Somewhere in the Evening' (and unlike the third character on stage, a distracting man-dog), she exhibits a refreshing and magnetic lack of capital-P Performance that helps to smooth over Leah Nanako Winkler (book) and Duncan Sheik's (score) oft-pedestrian writing more than any bit of glitz or shock.
I can't say that the focus allows any deep psychological insights, but it does give each of the principal cast members a time to show off their powerhouse vocals.

vr.q: The sexiest show in New York right now is happening in a lavish basement in Chelsea.
